_comment: THE HOUSE STANDARD. What every repository is expected to declare, per language.
WHY THIS EXISTS. Tooling lived in shell history. ruff has been the gate all
session -- run by hand, with default settings -- so csd-style-repair correctly
reported 'not configured by this repo' and skipped it. nl-router's CI runs
`uv run pytest` while our gate ran bare pytest, so a correct change was refused
three times with ModuleNotFoundError. An undeclared convention is one that only
exists while someone remembers it.
ADOPTION IS EXPECTED TO GO RED. Configuring a linter properly surfaces real
findings; that is the point, not a regression. Those are not the same as a gate
that fires on things which are not defects -- CI scrutiny demanding a run from a
workflow_dispatch-only workflow was a false positive, and 86 ruff findings are
86 real ones. Adopt, go red, fix the FIRST failure, re-run, repeat. After that
it stays green and stays enforced.
`required` blocks adoption from completing. `recommended` is reported and
queued as goals but does not block.

adoption._comment: One issue at a time, whatever fails first. A batch of 86 findings handed to an implementer produces a 3000-line diff nobody can review; one finding produces a PR a reviewer can actually judge.

package_manager.why: uv is the house manager. nl-router's CI runs `uv run pytest`, which installs the src-layout package first; a bare pytest cannot import it at all.

types.why: recommended: a repo with no annotations gains nothing from it on day one, but it is the third gate once lint and format are clean.

test.why: python_files as an ALLOW-LIST silently excluded 50 tests here, and the suite reported green for code it had never executed. Collect test_*.py and skip with a stated reason, never by omission.

python._toolchain: ruff is THE Python toolchain: it lints and formats, and its S rules are flake8-bandit. black, isort and flake8 are not listed because ruff already does their jobs -- five tools per language is five configs to drift.

package_manager.why: a committed lock file is what makes CI reproduce the local build

toolchain_pin.why: an unpinned toolchain means CI and the developer compile with different compilers, which is the Rust form of two definitions of correctness

rust._toolchain: the built-in Rust toolchain and nothing else: cargo, clippy, rustfmt.

lint.why: shellcheck has no fix mode; findings go to the implementer as tasks

typescript._toolchain: one per role: eslint lints, prettier formats, vitest tests.

_comment: ONE PATTERN, EVERY REPO. Divergent CI is how a repo goes green in one place
and broken in another. Three defects this session came from CI drift:
a guard on github.server_url that silently skipped every job for a week,
a hardcoded https:// URL job containers cannot reach, and a secret that was
never set so the token expanded to empty and the POST returned 401.

rules.why_never: server_url comes from the RUNNER's registered address, not ROOT_URL. A runner registered by IP made it false and every job reported `skipped`, which reads as success.
rules.why_never_hardcode: job containers cannot reach the public TLS edge; the runner-supplied address is the one that works
rules.why_token: the run's own token needs no rotation and cannot expand to empty; a managed secret that was never set returned 401 on every run
rules.why_no_installs: Baked into the base image is PREFERRED -- a runtime install costs wall clock on every run and makes CI depend on the network and on upstream availability. It is tolerated, not forbidden: a repo blocked from adopting the standard because fleet-ci-base lacks a tool is worse than a slow job, and that is exactly where this stood -- the rule forbade installs while the image carried neither uv nor ruff, so no repo could satisfy it.

parity.why: CI must be a near one-for-one reproduction of local validation. Two definitions of correctness is how a repo passes here and fails there -- gate_command() reads the repo's CI command for exactly this reason, but parity must be ASSERTED, not assumed.

house_rules.branch_and_pr: never push a trunk; working branch, PR, and merge only through the gates
house_rules.one_file_per_task: apply_proposal writes exactly one file per attempt, so a task spanning two lands half and closes anyway
house_rules.stubs: annotated with GOAL/BLOCKED/UNBLOCK/SEQUENCE, or INTENTIONAL: with a reason — see docs/AGENT-ORGANISATION.md
house_rules.style: repaired by the style role, never returned as a blocking finding
house_rules.secrets: via `secret exec VAR=name -- cmd`; never in argv, a URL, or a committed file
house_rules.commit_message: explain WHY, and name the failure that motivated the change
house_rules.file_extensions: every file carries the extension appropriate to its content, and a shebang that disagrees with the extension is a defect to fix, not to tolerate. Tooling keys off extensions: ruff walks *.py, so twenty extensionless Python scripts here were never linted and the repo reported clean.

extensions._comment: shebang -> required extension. A mismatch is scrutinised and fixed rather than worked around with an include list -- the include list is a patch over the real problem.
extensions._executables: a CLI that must be invoked without an extension gets a symlink or a console_scripts entry point, not a bare extensionless file
